bulgaria/alexander-nevsky.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and central Sofia
bulgaria/alexander-nevsky.description: The gold-domed cathedral and the compact centre of Sofia, with Roman ruins at Serdika.
bulgaria/alexander-nevsky.details: Alexander Nevsky is one of the largest Orthodox cathedrals in the Balkans, with a vast interior of mosaics and icons. The nearby centre holds the Roman Serdika ruins, the Banya Bashi mosque and the Sofia Synagogue within a few minutes walk. The area is easily explored on a free walking tour.

bulgaria/boyana-vitosha.name: Boyana Church and Vitosha mountain
bulgaria/boyana-vitosha.description: A medieval church with remarkable frescoes and a mountain park on the edge of Sofia.
bulgaria/boyana-vitosha.details: The Boyana Church is a UNESCO site with frescoes from 1259, well before the Renaissance. Entry is limited to small groups. Vitosha mountain offers a cable car and walking trails close to the city, giving a half-day outdoor option.

bulgaria/rila-monastery.name: Rila Monastery
bulgaria/rila-monastery.description: The largest and most famous monastery in Bulgaria, in a forest valley, with striped arches and frescoed church.
bulgaria/rila-monastery.details: Rila Monastery was founded in the tenth century and has a courtyard with arcades of black and white stripes and a church covered in frescoes. It is a UNESCO site two hours from Sofia. Monks still live there. Dress modestly, and avoid photography inside the church.

bulgaria/seven-rila-lakes.name: Seven Rila Lakes
bulgaria/seven-rila-lakes.description: A chain of glacial lakes reached by a chairlift and an easy hike in the Rila mountains.
bulgaria/seven-rila-lakes.details: The Seven Rila Lakes are a favourite mountain day out in summer, from about June to October. A chairlift from the road gives access, and a loop walk passes all seven lakes. The weather turns cold quickly and snow may remain into early summer.

bulgaria/melnik.name: Melnik wine village
bulgaria/melnik.description: The smallest town in Bulgaria, among sandstone pyramids, with cellars cut into the rock.
bulgaria/melnik.details: Melnik is known for its red wines, notably the local Shiroka Melnishka, aged in cellars dug into the hillside. Old Bulgarian houses line the lanes beneath sand pyramids. Tastings at family cellars are the main activity. The Rozhen Monastery is close.

bulgaria/plovdiv-old-town.name: Plovdiv old town and Roman theatre
bulgaria/plovdiv-old-town.description: A hilltop old town of Revival houses and a restored Roman theatre, one of the oldest living cities in Europe.
bulgaria/plovdiv-old-town.details: Plovdiv was a Thracian and Roman city. The Roman theatre still hosts concerts, and the old town on the hill has colourful nineteenth-century merchant houses, galleries and cafes. The cobbles are steep. The Roman stadium lies below the main pedestrian street.

bulgaria/kapana.name: Kapana creative quarter, Plovdiv
bulgaria/kapana.description: A lively district of craft shops, bars and street food beside the pedestrian centre.
bulgaria/kapana.details: Kapana means the trap, and the maze of small streets is full of artists, cafes, bakeries and cocktail bars. It is best in the evening. The area was renewed for Plovdiv European Capital of Culture year.

bulgaria/veliko-tarnovo-tsarevets.name: Tsarevets Fortress, Veliko Tarnovo
bulgaria/veliko-tarnovo-tsarevets.description: The ruined medieval capital on a hill above a river loop, the heart of the Second Bulgarian Empire.
bulgaria/veliko-tarnovo-tsarevets.details: Tsarevets is a fortified hill with walls, a patriarch church and the ruins of the royal palace, above the Yantra river meander. The old town lanes below are full of craft shops. A light and sound show lights up the fortress at night in season.

bulgaria/arbanasi.name: Arbanasi village
bulgaria/arbanasi.description: A hill village of fortified stone houses and richly painted churches near Veliko Tarnovo.
bulgaria/arbanasi.details: Arbanasi was a prosperous merchant village, and the Nativity Church has frescoes covering the walls and ceilings. The old houses behind high stone walls have been preserved. It is a quiet half-day trip with views and village restaurants.

bulgaria/koprivshtitsa.name: Koprivshtitsa museum town
bulgaria/koprivshtitsa.description: A hillside village of nineteenth-century houses linked to the 1876 April Uprising.
bulgaria/koprivshtitsa.details: Koprivshtitsa is a preserved village of coloured timber houses with bridges over a stream. Many houses are open as museums, and the village was where the uprising against the Ottomans began. It lies about 100 kilometres east of Sofia, and makes a pleasant stop between Sofia and Plovdiv.

bulgaria/rose-valley.name: Rose Valley and Kazanlak
bulgaria/rose-valley.description: A valley famous for rose oil and Thracian tombs, with a rose festival in early June.
bulgaria/rose-valley.details: Kazanlak lies in the Valley of the Roses, where Damask roses are harvested in May and June for oil. The nearby Thracian tomb is a UNESCO site, preserved in a replica for visitors. The Shipka Memorial Church is a golden-domed landmark on the pass.

bulgaria/nessebar.name: Nessebar old town
bulgaria/nessebar.description: A UNESCO peninsula town on the Black Sea with Byzantine churches and windmills.
bulgaria/nessebar.details: Nessebar is a small walled peninsula with ruined churches from the Byzantine era and wooden houses, joined to the mainland by a causeway. It is busy in summer, so go in the evening or in the shoulder season. The modern resort of Sunny Beach is nearby.

bulgaria/varna-sea-garden.name: Varna Sea Garden and archaeological museum
bulgaria/varna-sea-garden.description: The seaside capital with a long park, the beach and the museum that holds the oldest gold treasure in the world.
bulgaria/varna-sea-garden.details: The Varna Archaeological Museum displays the Varna Necropolis gold, the oldest worked gold known, from about 4,500 BC. The Sea Garden runs for kilometres above the beach. The Roman baths and the cathedral are in the centre. Beaches are busy from June to August.

bulgaria.name: Bulgaria
bulgaria.description: A Balkan country of monasteries, Thracian history, mountains and a Black Sea coast.

bulgaria/sofia.name: Sofia
bulgaria/sofia.description: The capital, with a golden cathedral, Roman ruins and mountains nearby.

bulgaria/blagoevgrad.name: Blagoevgrad
bulgaria/blagoevgrad.description: The south-west province of Rila, Melnik and the Pirin mountains.

bulgaria/melnik.name: Melnik
bulgaria/melnik.description: The smallest town in Bulgaria, a wine village below sandstone pyramids.

bulgaria/plovdiv.name: Plovdiv
bulgaria/plovdiv.description: A city of Roman ruins, an old town and a creative quarter.

bulgaria/veliko-tarnovo.name: Veliko Tarnovo
bulgaria/veliko-tarnovo.description: The medieval capital on a cliff above a river bend.

bulgaria/varna.name: Varna
bulgaria/varna.description: The Black Sea capital, with gardens, beaches and an archaeological museum.
